why.title: Why strategy consulting?
why.desc: In a fragmented European market where 70% of strategies fail to generate sustainable growth, tech leaders face critical choices: international expansion, operating model transformation, capital allocation between organic growth and acquisitions. Our approach combines strategic vision and operational execution to transform ambition into measurable results.

approach.title: Our approach

why.title: Why risk and compliance advisory?
why.desc: NIS2, DORA, the EU AI Act, the Cyber Resilience Act, the Swiss information security law: regulatory obligations have multiplied in two years, with shorter compliance deadlines and personal liability for executives. Many organisations discover their exposure at the worst possible moment, during an audit, a due diligence process or an incident. We help leaders document their compliance before it is required, and turn a regulatory constraint into a demonstrable advantage with clients, insurers and investors.

approach.title: Our approach
approach.desc: We do not deliver a theoretical compliance report. We map your actual exposure, document what already exists, and prioritise actions by their regulatory and commercial impact. Every recommendation is actionable, costed and assigned a clear owner.

steps.label: Regulatory mapping
steps.desc: Identification of the texts applicable to your organisation (NIS2, DORA, AI Act, GDPR/FADP, Swiss ISG, Cyber Resilience Act) based on your sector, size and location. Prioritisation by deadline and risk level.

steps.label: Compliance diagnostic

thoughtLeadership.title: Three complementary dimensions in a consolidating market
thoughtLeadership.desc: The European tech market is undergoing a structural transformation: technology is no longer a differentiating advantage, but a survival prerequisite. In this context, strategy, technology and M&A are no longer isolated disciplines : they form an inseparable triptych for leaders who want to grow.

pillars.label: Strategy: defining where to play
pillars.desc: Facing European market fragmentation and technological acceleration, leaders must make radical choices: which markets to address, which capabilities to develop internally, which acquisitions to target to fill gaps. Strategy defines the vision, but without a technology roadmap or M&A plan, it remains a dead letter.

pillars.label: Technology: building the advantage
pillars.desc: Technology has become the main differentiation lever: customer experience, operational efficiency, innovation capacity. But 70% of digital transformations fail due to lack of strategic alignment. A tech vision disconnected from business strategy generates technical debt and lost investments.

pillars.label: M&A: accelerating through consolidation
pillars.desc: Organic growth is no longer enough. European tech leaders consolidate their markets through acquisitions to gain critical mass, acquire rare talents, or accelerate their digital transformation. But without rigorous tech due diligence and IT integration plan, acquisitions destroy more value than they create.

thoughtLeadership.conclusion: Aegryn Advisory operates at the intersection of these three dimensions. We help tech leaders define a coherent growth strategy, build the technological capabilities to execute it, and identify acquisitions that accelerate the plan without creating technical debt. An integrated approach for a market that no longer forgives silos.

gradingSystem.label: Certification CIFSO 5000 : Methodology
gradingSystem.title:
Aegryn
Certification CIFSO 5000.
gradingSystem.intro: CIFSO 5000 is the first independent certification standard that assesses organizational value and transferability. Beyond operational compliance, it documents what makes an organization's real value: its intellectual capital, integrity, financial health, security, and organizational resilience.
gradingSystem.cifsDesc: Each asset is assessed across four independent dimensions, each scored from 0 to 25 points. The total score out of 100 determines the grade.

cifs.name: Code & Architecture
cifs.desc: Quality and governance of the technology base, proprietary code or licensed systems: architecture, maintainability, dependencies, reversibility. What makes the organisation transferable without dependence on its author. Reviewed by senior engineers.
criteria: Proprietary code quality and maintainability (tests, technical debt, vulnerabilities)
Licensed software governance: inventory, licences, supported versions
Reversibility and data export for critical solutions
Decoupled architecture or documented information-system mapping
Up-to-date technical documentation and dependencies

cifs.name: IP & Rights
cifs.desc: Trademark, software rights assignment, open-source licences, client and supplier contracts, litigation. The chain of title: what every partner checks first.
criteria: Trademarks registered in target jurisdictions
Software rights assignment signed (employees, contractors)
Third-party dependencies under compatible licences
Client and supplier contracts signed and archived
No active IP or contractual disputes

cifs.name: Finances & Metrics
cifs.desc: ARR, MRR, recurrence, churn, margins, cash flow, client concentration, growth history. All data verified against documents.
criteria: ARR documented over at least 24 months
Monthly churn < 3%
Gross margins > 60% (SaaS)
Runway ≥ 12 months
Annual ARR growth documented

cifs.name: Security & Sovereignty
cifs.desc: GDPR and LPD compliance, infrastructure security, access management, third-party audits, and AI exposure: provider inventory, sovereignty of data shared, client protection. Real control of assets and data.
criteria: GDPR / LPD compliance documented
MFA on all admin access, encryption at rest and in transit
Third-party security audit within the last 18 months
AI services inventory and formal usage policy
No client data sent to third-party AI models without contractual framework

cifs.name: Organisation & Talent
cifs.desc: Founder dependency, leadership team quality, succession plan, process documentation, transfer capacity. A company too dependent on its founder trades 20 to 30% below its intrinsic value.
criteria: Founder dependency ≤ 50% of revenue
At least one N-1 able to decide without the founder
Documented operational processes (runbooks, SOPs)
Formal succession plan for key roles
Turnover ≤ 15% per year over 2 years

gradingSystem.gradesDesc: Each grade corresponds to a precise score range and a distinct asset profile. AEG ★ and AAA grades are awarded to fewer than 15% of submitted assets.

grades.label: Exceptional
grades.profile: Exceptional asset. Reference architecture, strong IP, top-decile financial metrics, perfect compliance. A reference for institutional investors and partners.
grades.typical: B2B SaaS ARR > €2M, churn < 1%, test coverage > 90%, trademarks in 3+ jurisdictions.

dimensionRationale.C: Code level 1, test coverage >90%, mature CI/CD, near-zero tech debt, documented scalable architecture.
dimensionRationale.I: IP level 1, trademarks registered in 3+ jurisdictions, software rights fully assigned, no litigation, clear moat.
dimensionRationale.F: Finance level 1, audited ARR >€2M, NRR >120%, churn <1%, margins >75%, YoY growth >40%.
dimensionRationale.S: Security level 1, pentest <6 months with no critical vulnerability, full MFA, end-to-end encryption, documented GDPR/LPD compliance.
dimensionRationale.O: Organisation level 1: founder dependency ≤20% of revenue, autonomous N-1 on 2 key functions, documented succession plan, turnover <10%.

grades.label: Excellent
grades.profile: High-quality asset with solid fundamentals across all four dimensions. A few documented improvement areas but not blocking.
grades.typical: SaaS ARR > €500K, growth > 30% YoY, managed technical debt, full GDPR compliance.

dimensionRationale.C: Code level 1–2, solid tests (>70%), minor documented tech debt, functional CI/CD.
dimensionRationale.I: IP level 1–2, trademark registered, rights formalised, minor reservations possible on third-party licences.
dimensionRationale.F: Finance level 1–2, audited ARR >€500K, NRR >100%, growth >25% YoY, margins >60%.
dimensionRationale.S: Security level 1–2, pentest <12 months, MFA active, substantial GDPR compliance.
dimensionRationale.O: Organisation level 1 to 2: founder dependency <35%, at least one N-1 in place, partial operational documentation.

grades.label: Solid
grades.profile: Asset of fair quality with identified strengths and clearly documented areas for improvement. Eligible for transfer support.
grades.typical: Growing SaaS, some gaps in tests or compliance, IP in consolidation.

dimensionRationale.C: Code level 2–3, partial tests, tech debt identified and quantified, some documented improvement areas.
dimensionRationale.I: IP level 2–3, trademark in progress or locally registered, rights partially formalised.
dimensionRationale.F: Finance level 2–3, ARR documented >12 months, NRR close to 100%, stable growth.
dimensionRationale.S: Security level 2–3, existing security audit but >12 months old, partial GDPR compliance.
dimensionRationale.O: Organisation level 2 to 3: founder dependency identified and quantified, processes partially documented.

grades.label: Developing
grades.profile: Developing organisation with identifiable potential but structural weaknesses to address. Eligible for certification with a remediation plan.
grades.typical: Product in early traction, significant technical debt, partially documented financial metrics.

dimensionRationale.C: Code level 3–4, significant tech debt, insufficient tests, documentation to build.
dimensionRationale.I: IP level 3–4, trademark not filed or recent, rights to formalise.
dimensionRationale.F: Finance level 3–4, early traction (<12 months), metrics partially documented.
dimensionRationale.S: Security level 3–4, no recent audit, compliance to build.
dimensionRationale.O: Organisation level 3 to 4: high founder dependency, weakly structured team, no succession plan.

grades.label: Emerging
grades.profile: Early-stage asset with partial fundamentals. Certification accompanied by a detailed remediation report. Not eligible for transfer without improvement.
grades.typical: MVP or pre-revenue product, undocumented architecture, compliance to build.

dimensionRationale.C: Code level 4, undocumented architecture, uncontrolled tech debt.
dimensionRationale.F: Finance level 4, pre-revenue or minimal traction.
dimensionRationale.S: Security level 4, no compliance, no audit.
dimensionRationale.O: Organisation level 4: founder alone on all functions, no documentation, no succession plan.

gradingSystem.subcodesDesc: Each dimension receives a sub-code from M01 to M04 (Maturity) and D01 to D04 (Depth) specifying the exact level within the dimension.

principles.title: Strict separation
principles.desc: Aegryn analysts have no financial interest in the assets they certify. Any relationship with the holder or any interested party leads to automatic recusal.

principles.title: Reproducibility
principles.desc: Two independent analysts applying protocol v2.1 must reach the same grade to within ±1 sub-code. A greater discrepancy triggers an arbitration procedure.

principles.title: Traceability
principles.desc: Each grade is versioned. Any revision generates a new version with full history traceability. The original grade remains viewable.

principles.title: Coming reinforcement
principles.desc: Aegryn is progressively building a network of expert partners who can enrich certain reports with a complementary cross-review, as well as a blockchain certification layer to strengthen the traceability of the register. These additions will complement the already fully operational independent protocol, never replace it.

gradingSystem.refusalDesc: Certain configurations trigger an automatic refusal regardless of the overall score, the algorithm produces a score, the expert gives the final opinion, but an automatic refusal can never be overridden.
refusalConditions: Unresolved exposed secrets (C-40) combined with unresolved critical CVEs (C-34) → Code dimension refused
Active trademark dispute (I-18) or unformalised rights on third-party-produced codebase (I-21) → IP dimension refused
Unresolved critical vulnerabilities (S-17) or ongoing unresolved security incident (S-37) → Security dimension refused
Financial data not verifiable despite request → Finance dimension refused
Refusal to cooperate during the audit → Global certification refusal
Refusal to cooperate during the audit → Overall refusal of certification
gradingSystem.maturityDesc: Aegryn adapts its evaluation criteria based on asset maturity.

maturityRules.rule: ★/AAA/AA grade impossible on F. Grade C possible only if I=1 and C=1. Maximum AEG: A.
NRR not significant (period too short). F based on growth and unit metric quality (LTV:CAC, churn).
Full standard evaluation. All grades possible.
Audited ARR required for F-1 or F-2. NRR retention history over at least 4 quarters.
Valuation on tangible assets only. F dimension gets a special "Pre-revenue" note with no numeric score. Maximum AEG: A.

gradingSystem.fullCodesDesc: Each sub-code identifies a specific criterion evaluated during certification. Codes marked ⛔ are automatic refusal conditions.
gradingSystem.whyDesc: Existing standards certify systems and processes. CIFSO 5000 certifies value and transferability. These are two different, complementary objects, not competitors.

items.q: Who is Aegryn and what do you do?
items.a: Aegryn is a Swiss firm of entrepreneurs, anchored in Switzerland and open to the world. It frames the decisions and projects of SME and mid-sized company leaders (strategy, risk, finance, technology, operations, talent, project management, M&A), delivers them with you, accompanies every life cycle of the company, selects key profiles and keeps you informed on the market. La Boutique runs a limited number of signature projects. Our CIFSO 5000 protocol certifies and documents the value of an organisation.

items.q: What differentiates you?
items.a: A named contact who answers for the result, a limited number of mandates at a time, a reply within two working days, and independent experts coordinated when a subject requires it. We speak as entrepreneurs: a short deliverable that helps you decide or act, through to acceptance. Rare by selection, discreet by principle.

items.q: What are the certification options and their pricing?
items.a: CIFSO 5000 certification comes in three packages depending on the size of the organisation: Express (under 20 employees, single site) from €5,000, Standard (20 to 100 employees) from €9,000, Premium (over 100 employees or multi-site) from €15,000. All include the full audit across the five dimensions, the independent certification report, the official grade and registration in the Aegryn certified register. Prices exclusive of tax, indicative; final quote after pre-qualification.

items.q: What is the Aegryn Grade?
items.a: The Aegryn Grade is an official multi-dimensional certification assessing 5 dimensions: Code (C), IP & Rights (I), Finance (F), Security (S), Organisation (O). Each dimension is scored out of 20 points. The total score determines the official Grade: AEG ★ Exceptional (90+), AAA Excellent (75+), AA Solid (60+), A Developing (45+), B Emerging (30+).

items.q: What types of organisations can you support?
items.a: Aegryn works with leaders and organisations of all sizes, mainly SMEs and mid-sized companies, as well as investors, institutions, industrials and brands. CIFSO 5000 certification is aimed at tech organisations: B2B SaaS publishers, mobile applications, platforms, AI protocols, digital intellectual property assets.

items.q: Who accesses my certification file data?
items.a: Your data remains strictly confidential. A mutual, fully digital non-disclosure agreement precedes any detailed exchange. Only the Aegryn team and mandated auditors, all bound by that agreement, access your file, and access to certification and data-room sections opens only after signature and manual activation by Aegryn.

items.q: Do you support acquisition projects?
items.a: Yes. Acquisition projects are assessed within our Acquisition lifecycle support: independent due diligence, sovereignty audit, CIFSO 5000 certification of the target and integration plan. See /accompagner/acquisition or contact our teams.

items.q: What KYC documents are required?
items.a: Individuals: valid ID, proof of address less than 3 months old. Entities (companies, funds): company register extract or equivalent less than 3 months old, articles of association, ID of the legal representative, declaration of beneficial owners (UBO at 25%+), regulatory licence if applicable.

items.q: How does transfer support work?
items.a: Support follows the Transfer cycle: uncompromising diagnostic, CIFSO 5000 certification, data room preparation and coordination of the execution network. Details at /accompagner/transmission.

items.q: How does Aegryn guarantee grade traceability?
items.a: Each grade is documented, versioned and kept in the Aegryn registry. Any modification of the certified codebase after issuance generates a new version. This makes it possible to prove at any time that the code received matches exactly the certified code.

items.q: Do you offer talent selection services?
items.a: Yes, Aegryn Talent offers key-profile selection (executives and experts) and transition-profile placement, at every stage of the company lifecycle. Success-based fees due at start date, with a three-month replacement guarantee. Forms available at /talent.

items.q: What advisory services do you offer?
items.a: Aegryn Advisory covers eight disciplines: Business Strategy and Innovation, Risk Management and Compliance, Finance and Performance, Technology and Sovereignty, Operations and Operational Excellence, Talent and Organization, Project and Programme Management, M&A, Transactions and PMI. We work across more than 22 industries in Switzerland and Europe. See /advisory for details.

items.q: Do you build custom assets?
items.a: Yes, for bespoke software solutions that we steer end to end with experts: we scope the need, decide with you whether to buy, integrate or build, then lead delivery through to acceptance. Custom code only (no no-code), intellectual property fully transferred to the client, hosting in Switzerland or the EU. We do not ourselves carry out industrial production or physical manufacturing. Details at /advisory/technology.

items.q: What is the Aegryn magazine?
items.a: Quarterly publication on tech transactions, AI, exits and M&A trends in Europe. Available online at /magazine. Subscribe to receive upcoming issues 48h before release.

items.q: How to join the Aegryn expert network?
items.a: The Aegryn network brings together three circles: experts for the eight disciplines, investors and institutions, and independent CIFSO auditors. Independent professionals can apply through the Become a partner page (/alliances), Application section. Aegryn reviews each application and replies within 10 working days.

items.q: Do you offer organisation valuations?
items.a: Yes, via /valuation. Submit your organisation to receive a free indicative estimate. For a defensible valuation with a detailed report, CIFSO 5000 certification (Express, Standard, Premium packages) attests value across five dimensions.

items.q: Is Aegryn a marketplace or a transaction platform?
items.a: No. Aegryn is a firm of entrepreneurs: we advise and deliver. We operate no catalogue, no auctions and no buyer or seller area. Financial execution of an operation is entrusted to accredited partners.

items.q: What is La Boutique?
items.a: La Boutique is Aegryn's entrepreneurial boutique: we frame, deliver and accompany a limited number of signature projects end to end, for entrepreneurs, investors and family offices, institutions, industrials and brands. Discover it at /boutique. To entrust us with a project, write to us: a confidentiality agreement precedes any detailed exchange and the reply is personal, within two working days.

items.q: How does the non-disclosure agreement (NDA) work?
items.a: The agreement is mutual, fully digital and needs no account. Aegryn sends it to you manually through a personal link; you sign online and Aegryn countersigns automatically (named signatory, timestamp, document fingerprint). Additional signatories can be added. Access to certification and data-room sections then requires a signed NDA and manual activation by Aegryn.

intro.p1: neediu is a platform that enables users to quickly identify and connect with trusted professionals or individuals offering help with home-related needs in their area. As we place great importance on protecting your data and privacy, we have prepared this data protection notice to explain what we do with your data when you use our platform.
intro.p2: This data protection notice covers only data processing related to our platform. Our goal is to ensure adequate protection of personal data in accordance with all applicable data protection laws, including but not limited to the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP) and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
intro.p3: In Switzerland, the protection of your data is based in particular on the Federal Act of the 25th of September 2020 on Data Protection (FADP), as well as on the Federal Ordinance of the 31st of August on Data Protection (DPO). Our data protection notice, as well as our practices, is aligned with the legal provisions contained within the legislation mentioned.
intro.p4: Although we make every effort to simplify our data protection notice, the difficulty of understanding it stems from the language specific to the legal framework. This is why we have taken the initiative of grouping together the main definitions to make our data protection notice easier to understand, as these are taken from the FADP.

dataSubject: The natural person whose personal data is being processed.
personalData: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person.
sensitiveData: Data relating to religious, philosophical, political, or trade union opinions or activities; data relating to health, the private sphere, or racial or ethnic origin; genetic data; biometric data uniquely identifying a natural person; data relating to administrative and criminal prosecutions or penalties; data relating to social welfare measures.
processing: Any operation performed on personal data, including collection, recording, storage, use, modification, disclosure, archiving, erasure, or destruction.
controller: A private person or federal body that, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of processing personal data.
processor: A private person or federal body that processes personal data on behalf of the controller.
pfpdt: The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner, responsible for overseeing the proper application of federal data protection provisions.

whoWeAre.h: Who are we and how to contact us?
whoWeAre.p: Aegryn is the name of our company. If you have questions about data processing related to our platform, you may contact us by post: Aegryn , c/o Cofidex SA, Rue du Centre 142, 1025 St-Sulpice, Switzerland. You may also reach us via the contact form available on our platform.

ourRole.h: What is our role in data protection?
ourRole.p1: When you use our platform, we may process certain personal data about you. Under the FADP, we act as the data controller. When personal data is shared with a Service Provider for the execution of a task, the Service Provider acts as an independent data controller.
ourRole.p2: As data controller, we determine the purposes for which we process your personal data, how it is processed, and the applicable security measures. When we work with third-party providers in the course of our business, we ensure that they share our commitment to data protection and comply with the same standards we apply.
ourRole.p3: Data protection is everyone's business. We therefore encourage you to read our data protection notice. We also encourage you, if you are one of our customers, to review the contractual documents that bind us, as these may contain additional details about how we process your data.

whenCollect.h: When and how do we collect your data?
whenCollect.p: Data collection begins as soon as you access or interact with our Platform. We collect data directly from you when you use the Platform and when you create a User Account, whether as a Client or a Service Provider. We do not collect data from third parties, except in the context of targeted marketing campaigns, where a limited and indirect collection of personal data may occur. In such cases, data may be shared with us by third parties in accordance with their respective data protection notices.

categories.h: What categories of data do we process?
categories.contactP: Name, first name, address, phone number, or email address when creating an account.
categories.privateP: Data relating to your personal situation: gender, date of birth, photo, place of origin, contact language, and country of residence.
categories.accountP: Account status, services offered or requested, profile picture and other preferences, service history, availability settings, participation in features such as reviews or messaging.

sensitive.p: We do not collect or process any sensitive personal data.

minors.h: What about data relating to minors?
minors.p: Our services are intended exclusively for adults. We do not target minors and do not deliberately collect any personal data relating to them.

why.h: Why do we process your data?
why.p: We process your personal data to enable you to access and use the functionalities of our platform and to ensure the proper execution of the services offered through it. This includes, in particular, the creation and management of your user account, the connection between Clients and Service Providers, the processing of payments, the transmission of messages between users, and the display of relevant information based on your profile and preferences. We also process your data for the purpose of communicating with you, in particular to respond to your requests and exercise your rights, as well as to inform you about our services. We also process your personal data in order to generate traffic statistics that are useful for improving our platform. Finally, we process your personal data to comply with laws, directives and recommendations from authorities.

automated.h: Do we take automated individual decisions?
automated.p: We use various IT tools to manage our activities. These tools are designed to centralise and structure processes, improve efficiency and guarantee the quality of our services. It is important to note that we do not take any automated individual decisions with the help of these IT tools.

rights.pIntro: In general, the FADP grants you the following rights:
items: You have the right to access your data.
You have the right to request that your data be provided in a commonly used electronic format.
You have the right to have inaccurate data corrected.
You have the right to object to the processing of your data.
You have the right to request the deletion or destruction of your data.
You have the right to request that an automated individual decision be reviewed by a natural person.
rights.pContact: If you wish to exercise any of the above rights, please contact us. In order to prevent misuse, we must first identify you (e.g. by means of a copy of your identity card, if no other means of identification is possible). Please note that conditions, exceptions and restrictions may apply to the exercise of these rights under the FADP (e.g. to protect third parties or trade secrets). rights.pContact2: If you believe that we are processing your data in contravention of data protection provisions, you also have the option of reporting us to the FDPIC. security.h: How do we protect your data?
security.p: We take appropriate security measures, such as encryption, to keep your personal data safe and make sure it stays private, secure, and available. Unfortunately, we cannot guarantee that your data will always be completely safe. If you believe your personal data has been compromised, please let us know right away at legal@boha-group.com.

storage.h: Where and for how long is your data stored?
storage.p: Personal data is stored in our premises as well as in processing centres operated by our third-party providers. We retain it for as long as the purpose of processing requires, or as long as we have a legitimate interest in retaining it. For certain data, the retention period may be up to ten years. Once these periods have elapsed, we destroy your personal data.

sharing.h: Who do we share your data with?
sharing.p1: The management of our platform involves collaboration with specialised external third-party providers, particularly for its creation, maintenance and hosting. We collaborate with third-party providers recognised in their field of expertise to ensure the smooth running of our platform and, more generally, the quality of our services. Within the framework of these collaborations, it may be necessary to communicate your data to our third-party providers. Please be assured that these communications are strictly limited to what is necessary and are carried out in compliance with the legal framework.
sharing.p2: In addition, certain personal data is also shared directly between users when it is necessary for the preparation, execution, or follow-up of a requested service. Such exchanges are essential to enable the proper functioning of the platform and the services it facilitates.
sharing.p3: Where personal data is transferred to a third-party provider located outside Switzerland or the European Economic Area (EEA) and not offering an adequate level of protection, we require that the third-party provider undertakes to comply with the applicable data protection legislation (for this purpose, we use the revised standard contractual clauses of the European Commission), unless the third-party provider is already subject to a legally accepted set of rules designed to guarantee data protection (Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework) or we can invoke an exception.

brochure.coverSubtitle: The independent standard for certifying the value and transferability of organisations
toc: The added value for your organisation
brochure.s1Lead: Existing standards certify systems and processes. CIFSO 5000 is a quality audit of the valuation of a company's assets: it certifies the value and transferability of an organisation.
brochure.s1P1: A company can be fully compliant operationally and still be difficult to value, finance or transfer. Like a collector's watch without its papers, it loses part of its value for lack of proof. CIFSO 5000 closes this gap: it is the title deed of the organisation's value. It independently and verifiably documents what constitutes its real value: its code and architecture, its rights, its financial health, its security and sovereignty (including its exposure to third-party AI solutions), its organisational resilience. And it sets the reference value with the CIFSO Valuation Index as the source.
brochure.s1P2: The result is an official, versioned and defensible grade that can be presented to investors, acquirers, banks, partners or successors as third-party proof of the organisation's quality and transferability.
brochure.s2Lead: CIFSO 5000 is designed for executives and shareholders who need to demonstrate, defend or transfer the value of their organisation.

cifso.label: What CIFSO 5000 Certification documents
cifso.title: The Organisation dimension against this data.
cifso.body:
The CIFSO 5000 protocol assesses the Organisation & Talent dimension on precise, verifiable criteria: founder dependency (O-11), management team depth (O-12), succession plan (O-13), operational documentation (O-14), key talent retention (O-15, reference threshold: annual turnover at or below 10% on critical roles).

These criteria measure the stability of an organisation, not its capacity to keep pace with the skills recomposition shown by the data above. A team stable under criterion O-15 can still carry a skills gap if no update is undertaken: retention and skills refresh are not measured the same way.
